description: Measurement records of the experiments that the eight-stage runner does not produce. Each set is a directory records/<set>/ holding summary.csv (one measured value per row, each traced to the raw file it is read from), the raw logs under raw/, the code and configurations under code/, and provenance.json. scripts/records.py checks every value against its raw file and prints the supplementary table from the summary.

baselines.title: Per-rerun resource ledger and retrained baselines

quantities.wall_time: controller-branch wall time in nominal executions (nominal = 1)
quantities.gpu_hours: qualification or retraining GPU-hours from the scheduler accounting
quantities.score: official test metric of one optimization seed (percent or AP points)
quantities.hpo_trials: hyperparameter trials under the shared 48-trial ceiling

baselines.notes: Exported by scripts/export_records.py baselines from the pinned-upstream studies of scripts/run_upstream_baseline.py, the E17 timing rows (cm_campaigns.timing) and the original sacct exports. Rows without a seed carry per-method quantities; the score SD over the optimization seeds is computed from the per-seed rows.

quantities.official_metric: official test metric (percent or F1 points)

quantities.residual_activity: fraction of graphs or episodes with residual action activity
quantities.input_fallback: fraction of graphs or episodes returned by the input fallback

input_gate.title: Serving-time input gate and deployed latency

quantities.fallback_probability: fraction of test inputs returned to q_C by the input gate g_input
quantities.deployed_wall_overhead_percent: deployed latency after fallback relative to q_C (percent)

nominal_time.title: Per-input nominal execution time
nominal_time.notes: Exported by scripts/export_records.py from-runs (wall seconds of one nominal member execution per input, from the run's own execution record) or from E17 timing rows; provenance.json states which.

sensor_parameters.title: Executed sensor parameters

quantities.sketch_dim: executed sketch width k (0 = full-state sensing)

sensor_parameters.notes: The runtime separates spectral sensing_period from observer_period. Sealed config values and observed action counts are exported; trace counters record actual acquisitions. Manuscript observer period must not substitute for a missing sensing period.

quantities.route_stable_folds: outer folds selecting the reported route

ensemble_grid.title: Ensemble law on the extended grid

quantities.loss_nats: comparator loss of the E-member ensemble with the paired seed structure (nats)

ensemble_grid.notes: The table fits l(E) = l_inf + D_inf / E by least squares over the deposited ensemble sizes, as Supplementary Table S26b states.

budget_matched.title: Budget-matched arms at the common ceiling

quantities.effect_vs_qc_nats: mean paired loss of the arm minus q_C on the independent comparison units D_compare (nats)
quantities.effect_vs_feedback_nats: mean paired loss of the arm minus the confirmed feedback rule q_M (nats); positive favours q_M
quantities.effect_vs_feedback_ci_low_nats: lower end of the 95% crossed seed-by-unit bootstrap interval of the arm-minus-q_M effect (nats)
quantities.p_holm: Holm-adjusted two-sided paired sign-flip P value within the dataset's family of four arms
quantities.work_ratio: expected deployed work of the arm relative to q_C on the independent comparison inputs D_compare
quantities.ceiling: registered common ceiling (expected work relative to q_C)

budget_matched.notes: Exported by scripts/export_records.py budget-matched from a complete campaign export (scripts/arm_campaign.py export --complete). Every value is read from the campaign's analysis.json, which cm_campaigns.arm_campaign.check_campaign recomputes from the paired per-unit observations and the input-level work ledgers. The configuration key is 'selected': each controller replicate's development-selected configuration.

action_gap_audit.title: Action-gap and switching audit of the deployed rules

quantities.median_gap_nats: median over the executed decision sites of the deployed rule of the gap m_l between the best and second-best supported scores (main Proposition 3; nats)
quantities.p5_gap_nats: 5th percentile of the same site gaps (nats)
quantities.near_zero_threshold_nats: the near-zero gap threshold the audit applies (nats)
quantities.near_zero_fraction: fraction of decision sites whose gap is below near_zero_threshold_nats
quantities.switch_fraction: fraction of decision sites whose executed action changes when the state is perturbed by the registered perturbation (complement of mode-stable coverage)
quantities.recovery_index_stability: fraction of trajectories whose last-safe (recovery) index is unchanged under the perturbation
quantities.beam_sequence_stability: fraction of replanning sites whose planned beam sequence is unchanged under the perturbation; 1 for rules that do not plan
quantities.decision_sites: number of executed decision sites entering the audit

action_gap_audit.notes: Computed from per-site decision logs of the deployed rule on its evaluation role and from a perturbed re-execution of the same inputs. The lifecycle runtime records score_gap only for one-step/radius decisions of node-level member traces (member_predictions/*.json decisions[]); MPC-RH beam decisions, per-graph decisions of the multigraph benchmarks and every perturbed re-execution are not recorded, so the exporter must write the raw per-site gaps and switches.

band_bound_tightness.title: Tightness of the band-limited displacement bound

quantities.displacement_ratio: exact one-step displacement of the registered action divided by the band-limited bound (6.1), at states whose spectral energy density is proportional to exp(-lambda/lambda_0) on [0, 2] (ratio)

band_bound_tightness.notes: Keys: action = registry identifier A1 ... A7; spectral_scale = lambda_0 of the state's spectral energy density. A ratio above one falsifies an assumption of main Proposition 6 for that plant. The displacement and bound arrays of every evaluated state go under raw/; deposit with `python -B scripts/export_records.py from-mapping --mapping <band_bound_tightness mapping>` once the set is registered for the mapping exporter.

band_power_audit.title: Spectral displacement audit of main Proposition 6

quantities.tightness_ratio: transport displacement over the ideal six-band bound of Proposition 6(i) in the symmetric realization of L_sym: exact at a model density exp(-lambda/lambda0) (spectrum lambda0=...), median over audited states with an exact spectrum (spectrum explore_states) (ratio)
quantities.tightness_ratio_max: maximum of that ratio over audited states with an exact spectrum; a value above one falsifies a hypothesis of Proposition 6 for the plant (ratio)
quantities.window_bound_ratio: median over audited states of the transport displacement in the executed row-stochastic realization over the complete computable bound from the six Chebyshev windows with their approximation errors (ratio)
quantities.retained_statistic_ratio: median over audited states of the symmetric-realization transport displacement over the retained three-window statistic the controller measures (ratio)
quantities.omitted_band_share: median over audited states with an exact spectrum of the share of the squared ideal bound carried by the three bands outside the registered windows (fraction)
quantities.approximation_error_share: median over audited states of the share of the squared window bound contributed by the window approximation errors eps_b ||D^1/2 H||^2 (fraction)
quantities.degree_factor: median over audited states of ||X|| / (d_min^-1/2 ||D^1/2 X||), the used part of the degree weighting of the row-stochastic realization (ratio)
quantities.update_gain_p95: 95th percentile over audited states of the one-step block displacement ||H_l+1(a) - H_l+1(nominal)|| over the transport displacement (ratio)
quantities.logged_statistic_ratio: median over audited states of the full-state retained statistic over the reachability coordinate logged in the sealed D_explore record; one without sketching (ratio)
quantities.exact_spectrum_states: audited (state, action) pairs on graphs with an exact spectrum (pairs)
quantities.ranking_spearman: median over audited states of the Spearman correlation across A1-A7 between the retained statistic and the observed block displacement (correlation)
quantities.replay_max_abs_deviation: maximum absolute difference between a replayed and the logged D_explore measurement (measurement units)
quantities.update_lipschitz_max: maximum over depths of the per-depth native-update constant: the largest block over transport displacement among actions with the nominal retention (ratio)
quantities.shared_weight_spectral_norm: spectral norm ||W||_2 of the frozen shared update acting on the message (ratio)
quantities.activation_lipschitz: Lipschitz constant of the plant's activation (ratio)

rows.model densities: baseline x A1-A7 x lambda0: tightness_ratio
rows.explore states: baseline x A1-A7 x explore_states: every per-action quantity
rows.plant: baseline all, action all, explore_states: ranking_spearman, replay_max_abs_deviation, update_lipschitz_max, shared_weight_spectral_norm (shared-update plants), activation_lipschitz

band_power_audit.notes: The lifecycle records only the controller's partial statistic (reachability_A1..A7 of every logged measurement), not the displacement it bounds, the omitted-band and window-approximation terms or the native-update constants. Produced by `python -B scripts/run_experiment_b.py band-audit plan --parent <run sealed through explore> --output <dir>`, `... band-audit run --plan <dir>/plan.json --device cuda --trust-local-checkpoints`, then `... band-audit export --results <dir> --hardware ... --period ...` (cm_experiments/band_audit.py): a label-free replay of sealed D_explore trajectories (recorded actions and last-safe anchors; every replayed measurement is compared with the logged one) and, at each audited state and each registered transport action against the next site's nominal transport (shared A0, native mean aggregation or inserted identity), the displacements through cross_morse.core.apply_transport and the frozen block, the exact spectrum of L_sym on graphs up to exact_max_nodes, and the registry's Chebyshev windows. Band suprema are taken on a fine grid and at the actual eigenvalues. The incremental policy value over matched confidence/history controls belongs to E7 and is not measured here.

buffer_sensitivity.title: Buffer sensitivity of descriptive admission on the single-graph benchmarks

quantities.clipped_effect_nats: clipped paired loss effect D_bar of the confirmed rule minus q_C on D_admit with the cores built at this buffer (nats)
quantities.half_width_nats: U_desc minus D_bar: one-sided half-width of the cluster-bootstrap interval at this buffer (nats)
quantities.upper_nats: U_desc: one-sided (1 - alpha) cluster-bootstrap upper limit of the clipped effect (nats)
quantities.admitted: descriptive admission decision at epsilon_a: 1 when D_bar <= -epsilon_a and U_desc < 0, otherwise 0
quantities.resampling_units: number of resampling units entering the cluster bootstrap at this buffer

buffer_sensitivity.notes: The released runtime cannot produce this set. cross_morse/data.py records the k-hop buffer as a context diagnostic only (buffer_role context_diagnostic_only; propagation on the full graph), and cross_morse.statistics.admission resamples the METIS or degree-stratified cores of prepared/clusters.npz, so data.buffer_hops changes no admission statistic. The paper states that the intervals widen with the buffer because the effective number of independent clusters falls, but does not define how the buffer enters the resampling units. The producing experiment must define that unit construction (and record resampling_units) before the set can be measured; scripts/run_sweep.py refuses the sweep until it exists. Rows are written by scripts/export_sweep_records.py from a sweep results file with these keys and quantities.

confirmation_contrasts.title: Contrasts of the nine-test confirmation family on separated confirmation data

quantities.effect_nats: paired loss contrast of the test (nats)
quantities.unit_count: number of statistical units entering the contrast

confirmation_contrasts.notes: One row per test of cm_campaigns.confirmation.FAMILY. Single-graph rows are the D_confirm tests; the multigraph rows are the validation-split contrasts at the original confirmation size J_old.

confirmation_sensitivity.title: Confirmation-size sensitivity of the multigraph mechanism contrasts

quantities.effect_nats: paired mechanism contrast at the validation-split size J_old (nats)
quantities.ci_low_nats: lower end of its 95% graph-bootstrap interval at J_old (nats)
quantities.units_old: graphs of the validation-split confirmation J_old (graphs)
quantities.graph_variance_share: share of the contrast variance attributable to graphs in the two-way seed-by-graph variance model of Note S24 (fraction)
quantities.holm_p: Holm-adjusted P value of the contrast in the nine-test family of Supplementary Table S14 at the D_confirm size (probability)
quantities.label_survival_probability: probability that the Holm-significant label survives at the D_confirm size under the two-way variance model (probability)

confirmation_sensitivity.notes: Keys are the contrast identifiers of cm_campaigns.confirmation.FAMILY for the three multigraph benchmarks (Pascal/RH, COCO/RH, Peptides/radius); that registry supplies the D_confirm sizes and the practical margins. The interval at the D_confirm size is computed from these quantities with fixed means (analytical sensitivity, not an observed replication). The paired per-graph arrays and the two-way variance fit go under raw/; deposit with `python -B scripts/export_records.py from-mapping --mapping <confirmation_sensitivity mapping>` once the set is registered for the mapping exporter.

decision_traces.title: Executed decision origins and within-depth action entropy of the deployed rules

quantities.same_depth_action_entropy: entropy (nats) of the executed actions among D_test decisions at the same controlled depth, averaged over depths with weights equal to their decision counts
quantities.fraction_schedule_nominal: fraction of D_test decisions taken from a fixed schedule or the nominal action
quantities.fraction_state_conditioned: fraction of D_test decisions chosen by a one-step or radius score of the current measurements
quantities.fraction_exclusive_sequence: fraction of D_test decisions taken from a receding-horizon planned sequence
quantities.fraction_recovery: fraction of D_test decisions that are registered recovery actions
quantities.fraction_input_fallback: fraction of D_test decisions on inputs returned to q_C by the input gate or by a global q_C return

decision_traces.notes: The five fractions of a dataset sum to one. Sealed runs keep per-decision origins only for whole-graph executions, so graph-level traces must be exported from the serving-time execution records.

depth_diagnostics.title: Depth diagnostics of the plants and deployed rules

quantities.source_alignment_change: mean source alignment c_lb over the retained bands at depth l minus its value at the first plotted depth, on the reference plant (D_fit validation)
quantities.policy_loss_change: paired CE/BCE of the selected policy truncated at depth l minus its value at the first plotted depth (nats)
quantities.first_intervention_depth_q25: 25th percentile over inputs of the first depth with a non-A0 action
quantities.first_intervention_depth_median: median over inputs of the first depth with a non-A0 action
quantities.first_intervention_depth_q75: 75th percentile over inputs of the first depth with a non-A0 action
quantities.supported_deterioration_depth: first depth after the plant's best-validation-loss depth whose paired loss increase over that depth has a 95% interval above zero
quantities.transport_fraction: fraction of executed sites of a depth phase (early, middle, late thirds) that carry a non-A0 transport action

depth_diagnostics.notes: Rows with a depth carry source_alignment_change (reference plant only) or policy_loss_change; rows with a phase carry transport_fraction; the other quantities carry neither, and the key 'all' stands for an absent depth or phase. First-intervention quartiles are taken over executions (ensemble member x input). The lifecycle records nominal depth losses (train/entry_initial.json) but no per-depth source alignment, no truncated-policy losses and no per-graph action sequences for the multigraph benchmarks. Produced by scripts/run_trajectory_audit.py depth (cm_experiments/trajectory_audit.py).

ensemble_grid_scores.title: Official scores on the comparator ensemble grid

quantities.official_score: official test metric of the comparator's E-member ensemble with the paired seed structure of the ensemble_grid set (percent or F1 points; AP in native units)

ensemble_grid_scores.notes: Companion of the ensemble_grid set (same checkpoints, same E grid 1, 2, 4, 8, 12, 16, 20 and the same test inputs): ensemble_grid holds the comparator loss, this set the official score of the same ensembles. Scores are recomputed from each ensemble's saved test predictions with the official metric (cross_morse.evaluation.score_observations) and written with the SHA-256 of the predictions under raw/; deposit with `python -B scripts/export_records.py from-mapping --mapping <ensemble_grid_scores mapping>` once the set is registered for the mapping exporter.

horizon_beam_sweep.title: Planning-horizon and beam-width sweep of MPC-RH

quantities.selection_effect_nats: nested cross-fitted D_select paired loss of the MPC-RH configuration minus the reconstructed comparator q_C (select/decision.json mean of the configuration's candidate; nats)
quantities.expected_serial_cost: deployed sparse/dense multiply-add work of the configuration on D_select normalized by one nominal E = 1 execution (select/candidates.json cost; nominal executions); equal to the expected cost because the released runner has no serving-time input gate
quantities.oracle_headroom_bound_nats: U(Delta_oracle) of the registered configuration: upper limit of the training-only D_explore oracle headroom (select/entry_complete.json headroom upper of the parent run; nats)
quantities.realized_fraction: selection_effect_nats divided by oracle_headroom_bound_nats (fraction of the headroom bound realized; main Proposition 4)

horizon_beam_sweep.configuration: MPC-RH at the profile and ensemble size of the parent run's deployed MPC-RH rule; the horizon sweep holds the registered beam width, the beam sweep holds the registered horizon
horizon_beam_sweep.notes: Produced by `python -B scripts/run_sweep.py plan --sweep horizon_beam_sweep --parent <sealed PascalVOC-SP run> --output <sweep>`, `run_sweep.py run --plan <sweep>/plan.json --data-root <datasets> --device cuda` (one lifecycle run per configuration outside the parent's registered horizons and beam width: run_cross_morse.py --config <variant> --stage prepare..select --resume), `run_sweep.py collect --plan <sweep>/plan.json`, then `python -B scripts/export_sweep_records.py --results <sweep>/results.json --hardware ... --period ...`. Configurations inside the parent's registry (horizons of controller.horizons at controller.beam_width) are read from the parent run itself; the others come from variant lifecycle runs whose configuration differs from the parent only in controller.horizons or controller.beam_width. The headroom denominator is the parent's for every row.

mechanism_contrasts.title: Held-out mechanism contrasts outside the nine-test family

quantities.effect_nats: paired D_confirm contrast of the dataset's strongest feedback configuration (nats): state = conditional state destruction minus intact; rh_minus_ol = MPC-RH minus MPC-OL at the registered horizon and ensemble size
quantities.interval_low_nats: lower end of the 95% interval on the dataset's registered statistical unit (nats)

mechanism_contrasts.notes: Required for every (dataset, contrast) cell of Figure 3a-b that neither the joint S14 family nor the deployed rule's own confirm/decision.json supplies; produced by the confirm-stage contrast code of cross_morse.pipeline on D_confirm.

module_ablations.title: Module-specific ablations and their observed signatures

quantities.loss_change_nats: paired loss of the ablated arm minus the complete module on the held-out contrast (nats; positive means the module lowers the loss)
quantities.warning_lead_change_depths: change of the warning lead (controlled depths between the first warning and the onset of deterioration), ablated minus complete
quantities.false_safe_rate_change: change of the false-safe rate (executed decisions marked safe whose paired loss increased), ablated minus complete
quantities.risk_rmse_change: change of the held-out RMSE of the one-step risk model (nats), ablated minus complete
quantities.action_entropy_change: change of the entropy of the executed action mix (nats), ablated minus complete
quantities.innovation_rmse: held-out innovation RMSE of the observer variant
quantities.clean_score_change: change of the official score on supported inputs, ablated minus complete
quantities.worst_harm_change_nats: change of the worst per-unit paired loss harm, ablated minus complete (nats)
quantities.retained_effect_fraction: effect of the ablated arm as a fraction of the complete module's effect against q_C
quantities.cost_fraction: added cost of the ablated arm over q_C as a fraction of the complete module's added cost over q_C

modules.label: spectral bands
modules.failure_targeted: predictive deterioration not visible in confidence
modules.comparison: full sensors vs no bands/scrambled bands
modules.removal_rule: remove if no incremental warning or policy value
modules.runtime: unsupported: cross_morse.core.MeasurementBank requires exactly three distinct bands of the six-window bank (sensor.bands), and the Lean profile zeros the band-power, source-alignment and reachability coordinates together, so neither a band-only deletion nor a band scramble at matched capacity is configurable

modules.label: source alignment
modules.runtime: unsupported: no configuration key removes the three source-alignment coordinates of the measurement vector alone

modules.label: confidence sensors
modules.runtime: unsupported: entropy and margin are fixed coordinates of the measurement vector and also define the support strata

modules.label: transport history
modules.runtime: unsupported: accumulated mass and expected range are fixed measurement and observer-design coordinates

modules.label: observer
modules.runtime: unsupported: the runtime fits only the conditioned observer (cross_morse.learning.ConditionedObserver); raw, EMA and global observers have no configuration key

modules.label: radius uncertainty
modules.removal_rule: classify as one-step if radius fails
modules.runtime: post-hoc: radius-minus-one-step contrasts on D_confirm (confirm/decision.json); loss change = minus the contrast mean

modules.label: sequence risk
modules.removal_rule: remove replanning label if no value
modules.runtime: post-hoc: on runs whose deployed rule is MPC-RH, the nested D_select effect of the one-step route (critic only, no transition, stage or terminal model) minus that of the deployed MPC-RH configuration at the same profile and ensemble size (select/decision.json)

modules.label: recovery type
modules.runtime: unsupported: the source reset A8 and last-safe recovery A9 are fixed registry actions and cross_morse.policies.recovery_action has no configuration key

modules.label: comparator branch
modules.runtime: unsupported: the released runner has no serving-time input gate, so the comparator branch cannot be switched

modules.label: Full/Lean profile
modules.runtime: post-hoc: Full-minus-Lean retained-fraction contrasts on D_confirm (confirm/decision.json; Lean retains one minus the contrast mean) and the added cost of the Lean predecessor over q_C as a fraction of the Full rule's (select/candidates.json)

module_ablations.notes: Rows with dataset 'pooled' hold a pooled value; per-dataset rows are summarised as a range. Produced by `python -B scripts/run_sweep.py collect --sweep module_ablations --parent <run> ... --output <sweep>` for the three modules the released runtime supports (radius uncertainty, sequence risk, Full/Lean profile), then `python -B scripts/export_sweep_records.py --results <sweep>/results.json --hardware ... --period ...`. The other seven modules need runtime support that the release does not have; each module's 'runtime' field states what is missing.

oracle_dispersion.title: Per-input oracle enumerated on the admission split

quantities.median_oracle_depth: median over admission inputs of the depth of the per-input loss-minimizing sequence in the enumerated family
quantities.oracle_depth_q25: 25th percentile of the per-input oracle depth
quantities.oracle_depth_q75: 75th percentile of the per-input oracle depth
quantities.fraction_differs_from_qc: fraction of admission inputs whose oracle sequence differs from q_C

oracle_dispersion.notes: Diagnostic enumerated on D_admit after every decision is fixed (convention C12). The lifecycle records only the D_explore global-candidate headroom (select/entry_complete.json), not a per-input oracle on the admission split.

predictability.title: Predictability of the feedback policy's executed sequences

quantities.phi_seq: share of the frozen teacher q_M's executed (input, ensemble member) sequences on D_compare that the initial-input predictor reproduces exactly, terminal depth included, against the teacher sequence with dynamic A9 written as source-reset A8 (fraction)
quantities.phi_gain: paired share of the feedback gain retained by executing the predicted sequences: [R(q_C) - R(q_pred)] / [R(q_C) - R(q_M)] with every risk on the same D_compare units and the same frozen teacher (Note S25); absent when the measured feedback gain is not positive (fraction)
quantities.feedback_gain_nats: g = R(q_C) - R(q_M): unit-weighted mean D_compare loss of the locked comparator minus the confirmed feedback teacher (nats)
quantities.predictor_gain_nats: R(q_C) - R(q_pred): unit-weighted mean D_compare loss of the comparator minus the executed predicted sequences (nats)
quantities.compared_sequences: teacher sequences compared: D_compare inputs times ensemble members (sequences)
quantities.evaluation_units: statistical units scored on D_compare: complete graphs or graph cores (units)

predictability.predictor: the E4 distillation recipe of cm_experiments.schedules: fit_decoder(arm='E4') on the confirmed teacher's executed D_explore sequences and terminal depths (dynamic A9 rewritten to A8), capacity matched to the teacher's action critic, decoded once from the initial input (pooled H0 and four graph statistics) with the support mask of cm_experiments.execution.execute_arm and executed open loop
predictability.notes: Produced by `python -B scripts/run_experiment_b.py predictability plan --parent <run sealed through confirm> --output <dir>`, `... predictability run --plan <dir>/plan.json --device cuda --trust-local-checkpoints`, then `... predictability export --results <dir> --hardware ... --period ...` (cm_experiments/predictability.py). The predictor is fitted on D_explore and evaluated on the reserved D_compare against the same frozen q_M and q_C as E3-E6. phi_seq is descriptive; phi_gain is the quantity compared with the crossovers of Table S47 (Proposition 10). On a single transductive graph the predictor is fitted and evaluated on the same input with different label rows, so the readouts do not measure unseen-input generalization. Roman-empire splits are pooled by their mean risks when several sealed runs are exported together. The analytical retained-share grids of Tables S30, S33 and S47 are a separate sensitivity model and are not filled from this set.

reliability_diagnostics.title: Reliability, harm and fallback diagnostics

quantities.coverage: fraction of executed decisions or sequences whose realized consequence lies inside the predicted risk radius at the prediction horizon of the level (fraction)
quantities.coverage_ci_low: lower end of the 95% interval of that coverage (fraction)
quantities.risk_rmse: held-out RMSE of the one-step risk prediction made through the observer variant of the level (nats)
quantities.nis_coverage: fraction of held-out innovations of the observer variant whose normalized innovation squared lies inside the registered chi-square acceptance region (fraction)
quantities.false_safe_rate: executed decisions predicted safe whose paired loss increased, over executed decisions (fraction)
quantities.false_safe_ci_low: lower end of the 95% interval of the false-safe rate (fraction)
quantities.harm_miss_rate: executed decisions with a paired loss increase that the risk model did not flag, over harmful executed decisions (fraction)
quantities.harm_miss_ci_low: lower end of the 95% interval of the harm-miss rate (fraction)
quantities.input_fallback: fraction of deployment graphs or episodes returned to q_C by g_input (fraction)
quantities.residual_activity: fraction of deployment graphs or episodes with residual action activity (fraction)

diagnostics.coverage: level = prediction horizon in control depths (1, 4, 8, 16, 32); quantities coverage, coverage_ci_low, coverage_ci_high
diagnostics.observer: level = observer variant (raw, EMA, global KF, conditioned KF); quantities risk_rmse, nis_coverage
diagnostics.harm: level = dataset (the seven benchmark names); quantities false_safe_rate, false_safe_ci_low, false_safe_ci_high, harm_miss_rate, harm_miss_ci_low, harm_miss_ci_high, with the units of Supplementary Table S37
diagnostics.stress: level = clean (supported deployment inputs, the reference of the four negative_controls constructions); quantities input_fallback, residual_activity

reliability_diagnostics.notes: Coverage, observer consistency and harm accounting of the deployed rules, from the decision logs and held-out trajectories of the lifecycle runs and the observer-variant comparison of Supplementary Table S17 (the observer risk RMSE is the same measurement as module_ablations/innovation_rmse; both summaries may trace to one raw file). The runtime records sequence coverage as NOT_MEASURED (fit/<profile>/calibration_assessment.json), so these values come from the separate reliability evaluation; deposit with `python -B scripts/export_records.py from-mapping --mapping <reliability_diagnostics mapping>` once the set is registered for the mapping exporter.

runtime_scaling.title: Runtime and memory of the deployed rule against processed graph size

quantities.processed_edges_millions: edges processed by one execution of the deployed rule on the instance under the implemented scheduling (millions)
quantities.wall_time_seconds: synchronized wall time of that execution after warm-up, mean over the post-warm-up repeats (s)
quantities.peak_memory_gib: peak accelerator memory of that execution (GiB)

runtime_scaling.notes: One instance per timed graph: a full benchmark graph or a registered subgraph of the scaling sweep, named by the instance key. Timed with the E17 sessions of cm_campaigns.timing inside completed GPU allocations; the peak memory is read with torch.cuda.max_memory_allocated after a reset before each timed execution, and the processed-edge count is the operator's own count of the edges it visits. The timing rows, memory readings and scheduler exports go under raw/; deposit with `python -B scripts/export_records.py from-mapping --mapping <runtime_scaling mapping>` once the set is registered for the mapping exporter.

search_enumeration.title: Search versus model error by exact enumeration at H <= 4

quantities.two_e_H_nats: 2 e_H of main Proposition 8: twice the stated-confidence quantile over planning instances of the maximum over the enumerated supported family of |J_hat(a) - J(a)|, with the critic sigma penalty identical in both objectives (nats)
quantities.zeta_H_nats: zeta_H of main Proposition 8: stated-confidence quantile over planning instances of J_hat(beam sequence) - min over the enumerated family of J_hat (nats)
quantities.realized_regret_nats: stated-confidence quantile over planning instances of J(beam sequence) - min over the enumerated family of J (nats)
quantities.bound_coverage: fraction of planning instances whose realized regret is at most 2 e_H + zeta_H at the pooled values (fraction)
quantities.beam_optimal_fraction: fraction of planning instances on which the registered beam returns a minimizer of J_hat over the enumerated family (fraction)
quantities.two_e_H_zero_uncertainty_nats: 2 e_H with the critic sigma term set to zero in the true objective J (nats)
quantities.mean_family_size: mean number of enumerated supported sequences per planning instance (sequences)
quantities.planning_instances: planning instances (input, member, depth) with a complete enumeration and a returned beam sequence (instances)

registered.label_role: D_select for independent-graph benchmarks, D_explore for single-graph benchmarks

search_enumeration.notes: Produced by `python -B scripts/run_experiment_b.py search-enumeration plan --parent <run sealed through fit> --output <dir>`, `... search-enumeration run --plan <dir>/plan.json --device cuda --trust-local-checkpoints`, then `... search-enumeration export --results <dir> --hardware ... --period ...` (cm_experiments/search_enumeration.py). Planning states come from the released runtime: the initial measurement (MPC-OL) or the parent's registered MPC-RH policy executed by cross_morse.policies.execute_policy and replayed with its recorded actions and last-safe anchors. The family is every sequence the registered beam could expand without its top-k or beam-width truncation; J_hat uses beam_plan's exact arithmetic (Eq. 17, kappa = 1), J replaces the stage costs and the nominal-suffix terminal value by the frozen plant's measured loss changes on the declared label role. e_H is a supremum over the enumerated family per instance; the record states its stated-confidence quantile over instances (Note S20). The objective of single-graph benchmarks is evaluated on D_explore rows, the targets the consequence models were fitted to estimate.

sensitivity_grids.title: Registered sensitivity grids of support, selection and admission

quantities.qualified_fraction: fraction of the registered (stratum, action) support cells of the full-profile controller that qualify at this setting (per-cell minimum propensity, ESS and maximum normalized weight of fit/full/audit.json)
quantities.strata_without_transport: number of registered strata in which no action other than A0 qualifies at this setting
quantities.eligible_count: |Q_s|: feedback candidates satisfying main Eq. (19) at this setting
quantities.selected_complexity: registered complexity C(q) of the selected route (the provisional route, or q_C when Q_s is empty)
quantities.route_changed: 1 when the selected route differs from the route selected at the registered setting, otherwise 0
quantities.route_simpler: 1 when the selected route is lexicographically simpler (complexity, ensemble, cost) than the route selected at the registered setting, otherwise 0
quantities.clipped_fraction: fraction of admission units whose paired loss difference exceeds the clip level in absolute value
quantities.clipped_mean_nats: clipped paired effect D_bar on D_admit (nats)
quantities.admission_upper_nats: U_a (empirical-Bernstein upper limit, independent graphs), U_desc (cluster-bootstrap upper limit, buffered cores) or the repeated-split t upper limit (Roman-empire) of the clipped effect (nats)
quantities.raw_maximum_harm_nats: largest unclipped paired loss difference on D_admit (nats)
quantities.admitted: admission decision G_admit at this clip level (1 admitted, 0 comparator returned)

p_min.label: minimum propensity
p_min.measurement: support recomputation from the per-cell statistics (exact) and lifecycle variant runs through select (route)
p_min.required_report: qualified fraction, coverage, harm, fallback, compute

n_min.label: minimum ESS
n_min.measurement: support recomputation from the per-cell statistics (exact) and lifecycle variant runs through select (route)

max_normalized_weight.label: maximum normalized weight
max_normalized_weight.measurement: support recomputation from the per-cell statistics (exact) and lifecycle variant runs through select (route)
max_normalized_weight.required_report: support, FSR, HMR, route per joint cell

epsilon_r.label: selection margin εR
epsilon_r.measurement: main Eq. (19) re-applied to the sealed simultaneous upper limits of select/decision.json (exact; the limits do not depend on the margins)

epsilon_eq.label: equivalence margin εeq
epsilon_eq.measurement: main Eq. (19) re-applied to the sealed simultaneous upper limits of select/decision.json (exact)

clip.label: clip B
clip.measurement: cross_morse.statistics.admission replayed on admit/paired_units.npz with the stage's seed and replicates (exact)

sensitivity_grids.aggregation: Roman-empire: every quantity is the mean over the ten official split runs; per-split values are kept in the raw computed file, and the repeated-split admission upper limit is the small-sample t limit over the per-split clipped effects.
sensitivity_grids.notes: Produced by `python -B scripts/run_sweep.py plan --sweep sensitivity_grids --parent <run> ... --output <sweep>` (support-threshold variants are lifecycle runs: run_cross_morse.py --config <variant> --stage prepare..select --resume), `run_sweep.py run --plan <sweep>/plan.json --data-root <datasets> --device cuda`, `run_sweep.py collect --plan <sweep>/plan.json` (margins, clip and support masks are recomputed exactly from the sealed parent outputs), then `python -B scripts/export_sweep_records.py --results <sweep>/results.json --hardware ... --period ...`. One parameter varies at a time; the others stay at their registered values.

timing_anchors.title: Timing anchors that bracket the per-input nominal execution time

quantities.throughput_anchor_seconds: per-input nominal execution time implied by the multiply-add count W_nom of one nominal member execution at the sustained throughput measured for the plant on the deployment device (s); full-batch plants with a native dense layer only
quantities.training_anchor_low_seconds: lower end of the per-input forward-time bracket derived from the measured training time of one plant seed (s)

timing_anchors.notes: Anchors are adopted timing references, kept apart from the measured t_nom of the nominal_time set. Each dataset carries its own anchors, also when Table S23b prints another plant's anchor as the reference range (COCO-SP shares the PascalVOC-SP anchor because the two plants have the same backbone, depth and graph size; the generator applies that convention). The throughput and training-time records (scheduler accounting of the plant seeds, epochs and training inputs, and the sustained-throughput measurement) go under raw/; deposit with `python -B scripts/export_records.py from-mapping --mapping <timing_anchors mapping>` once the set is registered for the mapping exporter.

tube_audit.title: Plug-in trajectory-tube audit of main Proposition 2

quantities.beta_median: median over depths and audited trajectories of the plug-in factor beta_l
quantities.beta_p95: 95th percentile over depths and audited trajectories of beta_l
quantities.m_eps_op: median over depths of the plug-in operator term M_l eps_l^op
quantities.reference_term: median over depths of the plug-in reference term R_l e_l^ref
quantities.tube_coverage: fraction of audited trajectories whose realized state error stays inside the tube at every depth
quantities.mode_stable_coverage: fraction of audited trajectories whose realized and predicted runs keep the same action, recovery mode and last-safe index at every depth (the fixed-mode condition of Proposition 2)
quantities.final_bound_nats: product-sum tube bound of Proposition 2 at the final depth with the empirical per-depth constants, sqrt(2) ||W_head||_2 e_L (cm_theory.stability.unrolled_bound and logit_loss_bound; nats)
quantities.observed_error_median_nats: median over audited D_explore trajectories of |predicted minus realized loss| at the final depth (nats)
quantities.observed_error_p95_nats: 95th percentile of the same observed loss error (nats)

tube_audit.notes: One row per audited dataset. Computed from audited D_explore episodes of the deployed rule: a predicted (registered, undisturbed) run and a realized run under the declared input and edge-weight disturbance (provenance.perturbation), replayed jointly step by step; the per-depth constants beta_l, M_l, eps_l^op, R_l and e_l^ref are kept as raw arrays. The runtime records none of them. The violation rate of Table S22 is 1 - mode_stable_coverage (convention C22). main_paper.py reads final_bound_nats and the two observed-error quantities of the same rows. Produced by scripts/run_trajectory_audit.py tube (cm_experiments/trajectory_audit.py).
